transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this review meeting to go over the engagement of Atlas IP Litigation as outside trial counsel for the patent-infringement complaint we expect to file next month. As you know, Atlas's initial proposal lists an hourly rate of $425 and an estimated matter budget of $260,000. Before I record a binding decision on engagement terms, I'd like to hear from conflicts counsel and procurement on your respective findings and any recommended engagement conditions. Let's start with conflicts counsel — what did your review uncover?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, my conflicts review uncovered a significant issue. Atlas's completed conflicts questionnaire shows that Atlas currently advises a company whose confidential product roadmap is relevant to our planned patent case. My conflicts memo is still awaiting a final ethics classification, but based on what I've found, Atlas may be engaged only after that company gives written informed consent. Even then, we would need to impose an ethical wall barring the conflicted lawyers from this matter and a prohibition on using that company's confidential information. I cannot recommend proceeding with engagement until these conditions are satisfied.

transcript.text: Elena, on the procurement side, I checked our company's approved-firm pricing benchmark and confirmed that comparable patent-litigation work is approved at exactly $350 per hour with a not-to-exceed matter cap of $210,000. I received this benchmark confirmation from finance yesterday, though I haven't yet uploaded it to the procurement intake file. Atlas's proposed rate of $425 per hour and $260,000 budget both exceed our approved benchmarks significantly — $75 per hour over the approved rate and $50,000 over the approved matter cap. I'd recommend we negotiate Atlas down to the benchmark terms, or at minimum require justification for any deviation above $350 per hour and $210,000 before engagement is approved.

decisions.approval_status: conditionally approved pending satisfaction of conflicts and pricing conditions

commitments.detail: Engagement is conditional on Atlas obtaining written informed consent from the company whose confidential product roadmap is relevant to our patent case, as identified in the conflicts review.
An ethical wall must be established barring the conflicted Atlas lawyers from this matter.
Atlas is prohibited from using the other company's confidential information in connection with our matter.
Atlas's hourly rate must be negotiated down to $350 per hour, consistent with our approved-firm pricing benchmark for comparable patent-litigation work.
The matter budget not-to-exceed cap is set at $210,000, consistent with our approved benchmark. Any deviation above this cap requires written justification before approval.
